channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Colombia: Hawkish BanRep tightening bias – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Dev Ashish notes that Banco de la República delivered a larger-than-expected 75bp hike to 12%, reinforcing a restrictive stance as inflation and expectations stay well above target.

item.title: Silver rebounds above $60 as softer US data, Warsh remarks weigh on the US Dollar
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) rebounds on Wednesday and trades around $60.35, up 3.19% at the time of writing. The white metal is supported by a weaker US Dollar (USD) following softer-than-expected US economic data and comments from Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh.

item.title: India: Nowcast points to slower expansion – DBS
item.description: DBS' Senior Economist Radhika Rao with data support from Daisy Sharma, highlights that India’s real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew 7.8% year-on-year in 1Q26, slightly below the revised 8.0% in 3QFY26.

item.title: Canada: Solid Q2 rebound supports cautious outlook – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada's (NBC) Kyle Dahms notes that the Canadian economy began Q2 on a stronger-than-expected footing, with real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) boosted by energy, manufacturing and construction.

item.title: United Kingdom: Balanced inflation and politics risk – HSBC
item.description: HSBC’s Willem Sels and Lucia Ku note that UK inflation remains above target but see risks as more balanced after the US-Iran interim peace agreement.

item.title: Eurozone: Price pressures keep ECB on alert – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Ralph Solveen notes that Eurozone inflation fell to 2.8% in June, mainly on lower energy prices, while core inflation eased to 2.4%. The bank expects overall inflation to stay close to 3% in coming months.

item.title: Gold rebounds above $4,000 as softer US data, Warsh remarks weigh on US Dollar
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) advances above the $4,000 psychological mark on Wednesday as the US Dollar (USD) eases following remarks from Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh and softer-than-expected US economic data.

item.title: Copper: Tariff delay tempers upside – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay and Bart Melek note that Copper remains under pressure as the missed June 30 Section 232 tariff update removes a near-term supply risk and weakens short-term momentum.

item.title: Breaking: US ISM Manufacturing PMI dropped to 53.3 in June
item.description: The Institute for Supply Management’s (ISM) data showed the Manufacturing PMI edging lower to 53.3 in June, down from May's print and analysts’ expectations of 54.

item.title: Swiss Franc gains as US Dollar eases on Fed Chair Warsh's remarks
item.description: USD/CHF trims gains on Wednesday as remarks from Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh weigh modestly on the US Dollar (USD). However, expectations for a Fed rate hike and a lack of clarity surrounding US-Iran negotiations keep the Greenback's downside contained.

item.title: Breaking: Fed Chair Warsh says they are not happy with inflation above 2%
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Chairman Kevin Warsh reiterated that he will not be giving forward guidance on policy, while participating at a panel at the ECB Forum on Central Banking 2026.

item.title: Gold: Forecasts cut but constructive case intact – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong have lowered their end‑2026 forecasts for Gold and Silver, citing a tougher near‑term macro backdrop with higher real yields, a stronger US Dollar (USD) and slower ETF demand.

item.title: What is keeping the Japanese Yen at 40-year lows as Tankan surges and authorities watch from the sidelines?
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) continues to trade near levels last seen in 1986 against the US Dollar.

item.title: British Pound: Inflation risk keeps rates curve elevated – ING
item.description: ING strategists Michiel Tukker and Padhraic Garvey highlight that Sterling markets remain highly sensitive to UK inflation risks, especially around near-term fiscal spending plans.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar declines amid US Dollar safe-haven demand, NFP focus
item.description: NZD/USD trades lower at 0.5660 on Wednesday, down 0.32%, reversing part of the previous day's rebound. The pair remains under pressure as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is weighed down by a more cautious market environment, while the US Dollar (USD) continues to strengthen.

item.title: Lagarde speech: Risks are more broadly balanced than a few weeks ago
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde speaks at a policy panel at the ECB Forum on Central Banking 2026.

item.title: European Central Bank: July risks reduced on softer data – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s analysts argue that softer June inflation data should significantly lower the risk of another European Central Bank (ECB) rate hike in July.

item.title: BoE's Bailey: Rate cuts off the table at the moment
item.description: While speaking at a policy panel at the European Central Bank's (ECB) Forum on Central Banking, Bank of Governor (BoE) Andrew Bailey acknowledged that they have a softening economy and labour market.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Softer footing risk as intervention fades – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research strategist Chang Wei Liang notes that USD/JPY has surged above the mid-162 area as markets probe Japanese authorities’ tolerance for further Japanese Yen (JPY) weakness.

item.title: US Dollar: Modest upside risk with Sintra focus – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s appearance at Sintra and upcoming United States (US) payrolls are key for the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: US equities: AI-led earnings support – HSBC
item.description: HSBC analysts Willem Sels and Lucia Ku argue that concerns over mega IPOs and stretched valuations in US equities are offset by solid earnings growth across most S&P 500 sectors, driven by AI-related demand.

item.title: Euro hits one-year low vs. British Pound after Eurozone inflation misses forecasts
item.description: The Euro (EUR) falls against the British Pound (GBP) on Wednesday after softer-than-expected Eurozone inflation data reduced expectations for another European Central Bank (ECB) interest rate increase this year.

item.title: Euro: ECB rhetoric and Warsh risk guide downside – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING argues the ECB is unlikely to drop its tightening rhetoric yet, even if a second September hike might be a mistake.

item.title: United States private sector employment rises 98K in June vs. 113K expected
item.description: Private sector employment in the United States grew by 98K in June, the Automatic Data Processing (ADP) reported on Wednesday. This print followed the 122K increase recorded in May and came in below the market expectation of 113K.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention talk and BoJ signals – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Jane Foley Senior FX Strategist discusses speculation that Japan’s Ministry of Finance could intervene in favour of the Japanese Yen as USD/JPY trades near levels last seen in 1986.

item.title: Japanese Yen consolidates at 40-year lows against USD amid high intervention risks
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) continues heading south against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday. The USD/JPY pair has eased to the 162.70 area after hitting a fresh 40-year high at 162.84, but remains above Tuesday’s high of 162.67, nearly 0.6% higher on the week so far.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Supported by BoP and RBI stance – DBS
item.description: DBS economist Radhika Rao reports that USD/INR has eased towards the mid-94 handle as India’s balance of payments (BoP) improves and commodity prices fall.

item.title: Mexican Peso: USMCA risks and Banxico stance – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts Dev Ashish and Brendan McKenna discuss how ongoing United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) review uncertainty is likely to prolong policy risk for Mexico and weigh on growth and capex.

item.title: US Dollar: Stronger outlook with steady Fed – HSBC
item.description: HSBC’s Willem Sels and Lucia Ku highlight that the new Fed Chair’s hawkish tone supports expectations that US policy rates will stay unchanged through 2026 and 2027, reinforcing Dollar credibility.

item.title: White House Adviser Hassett: It would be mistake to raise interest rates
item.description: White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said in a statement during the late European trading session on Wednesday that it would be a mistake for the Federal Reserve (Fed) to raise interest rates.
